notes: The affirmative develops robustness across measures, convergent reasons for valuable worlds, and graded successor-theory weighting; the skeptic develops representation invariance, predictive specificity, and comparison of complete packages. These are distinct responses to the frozen debate, not interchangeable prompts for further research.

The conditional first argument, value-convergence argument, and theory-weighting argument have different inferential structures. Skeptical passages separately diagnose redescription, retrospective flexibility, and mismatched comparison levels. Shared probability vocabulary and genuine logical parallelism are not treated as boilerplate.

Pro premise one is explicitly conditional rather than a claim that parameter robustness has already been established. The new material remains a disclosed hypothetical contribution, not evidence attributed to either speaker or input to scoring.
Lists, subordinate clauses, contrasts, semicolons, and colon punctuation were read directly. The complete corpus has no severe punctuation-drift flag; no punctuation was added to meet a quota.

All thirty-two card descriptions include the actual claim and inferential purpose. Critiques distinguish limited objections from stronger positive burdens, preserve frozen scores, and contain no shared six-word boilerplate at the current threshold.
